answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge an adaptive compute toll: each new identity must solve a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with how many identities share its behavioral fingerprint, like a bridge toll that grows steeper the more carts cross it. Honest agents pay once and keep a crystal-clear record of useful work, while an attacker cloning thousands of accounts faces an ocean of rising costs that swamps any fake reputation they could harvest before it ever pays off.
